title: Tevatron Meets Megatron: Expert-Parallel LLM Reranker Training on an Academic Budget
abstract: Training large dense and mixture-of-experts (MoE) rerankers is constrained by GPU memory and distributed-execution efficiency, which has kept academic reranker research largely on dense models. Tevatron trains rerankers through the Hugging Face Trainer with DeepSpeed and PyTorch FSDP1, a stack that stalls on three fronts: DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 has a known gradient-gathering failure on this path, FSDP1 full sharding is memory-safe but throughput-bound, and neither offers the expert parallelism (EP) that MoE training needs. We present Tevatron 3.0, which integrates Megatron-Core as a reranker training backend while preserving Tevatron's data processing, evaluation pipeline, and Hugging Face checkpoint format. For full-parameter dense 8B training, Megatron matches FSDP1 on BEIR-15 NDCG@10 with approximately 4% lower epoch time and twice the peak GPU memory under matched data-parallel and recomputation settings, and approximately 22% lower epoch time in its recommended configuration; it supports both LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning. Expert parallelism makes it possible to train a 30B-parameter MoE reranker (Qwen3-30B-A3B) on two nodes. A controlled study of architecture, LoRA, and distillation on BEIR-15, with three first-stage retrievers and Hugging Face and vLLM serving, shows that the MoE reranker matches dense-8B quality at less than half the activated parameters and at higher inference throughput. We open-source the framework and trained checkpoints.
